title: Application | Mobile | Global accessibility requirements | Visa Product Design System

blocks.t: Find application requirements for testing mobile experiences.

items: Vision support (APP-1)Custom display & text settings (APP-1-1)Support screen reader (APP-1-2)View titled (APP-1-3)
Physical and motor support (APP-2)Flexible orientation (APP-2-1)Motion control (APP-2-2)Multiple authentication methods (APP-2-3)
Diverse user needs (APP-3)App language (APP-3-1)Warn about timeout (APP-3-2)Extend timeout (APP-3-3)Use an automated testing tool (APP-3-4)

blocks.t: Text content adapts to Larger Text setting.

items: Adjust OS level settings for Larger Text: iOS: Settings > Accessibility > Display & Text Size > Larger Text On. Set the size to the third notch from the largest accessibility size (notch 8 of 11). Android: Settings > Display > Font Size and Style > maximum setting.
Confirm that all text content adapts when applied.
Pass: All text content adapts to larger text setting when applied.
Fail: Some or all text content does not adapt to larger text setting when applied.

blocks.t: VoiceOver/TalkBack can be used to successfully interact with the full app experience

items: Interact with the full app experience and task flows using VoiceOver/TalkBack.
Confirm that all functionality can be used easily and effectively by the screen reader.
Pass: All features and functionality can be easily and successfully used with VoiceOver/TalkBack.
Fail: Some features and functionality cannot be easily and successfully used with VoiceOver/TalkBack.

blocks.t: Each screen/view needs to be titled and the title needs to be an accurate and descriptive title for the content presented on that screen/view.

items: Navigate to each view using the screen reader.
Confirm that each view has a title read aloud by VoiceOver/TalkBack.
Pass: All views have a title that will be read by VoiceOver or TalkBack.
Fail: One or more views are not titled.

blocks.t: Content is not restricted to one orientation, unless that orientation is essential, to allow users to orient the device according to their needs and personal setup.

items: Enable setting to allow orientation to switch based on how the device is oriented.
Open the application being tested and confirm that each screen adapts to the portrait or landscape orientation change when the device is rotated between these orientations.
Pass: All content adapts to current orientation as expected.
Fail: Some content that does not fall under the exception criteria in assumptions does not adapt to the current orientation as expected.
NA: The full app experience falls under the exception criteria in assumptions.

blocks.t: When device motion is used to control the interface there is a way to deactivate it and operate the same functionality through UI controls instead

items: Determine whether device motion is used to control the interface.
If device motion is used to control the interface, confirm that there is a way to deactivate motion control and operate the same functionality through UI controls instead.
Pass: Motion input is used but it can be deactivated and an alternative is provided.
Fail: Motion input is used and cannot be disabled or an alternative to motion is not provided.
NA: Motion input is not used to control the interface.

blocks.t: User authentication must avoid relying on a cognitive function test by providing multiple means of filling in authentication information.
Ensure that authentication form fields allow any of the following:

items: The fields allow autofill of information.
Information may be pasted into the form fields.
Biometrics can be used to sign into accounts.
Pass: The authentication fields allow autofill of stored information OR information can be copied and pasted into the fields OR biometrics (fingerprints, facial-scan, etc.) can be used to log in.

Fail: The authentication fields do not allow autofill AND information cannot be copied and pasted into the fields AND biometrics cannot be used (for example: none of the pass criteria methods are used).
NA: The view does not require interaction to authenticate.

blocks.t: The application language can be programmatically determined

items: Use the screen reader to interact with the application content.
Ensure that the screen reader output matches the correct language for each language supported.
Pass: The screen reader output matches the language of the application.
Fail: The screen reader output does not match the language of the application.

blocks.t: Users must be warned prior to when a session times out and expires.
Confirm that users are warned prior to when a session times out and expires.

items: Pass: Session timeout warning occurs prior to session time out and expiration.
Fail: Session timeout occurs without warning.
NA: No session timeout is present.

blocks.t: When a session timeout warning occurs, users MUST be given at least 30 seconds to take action in order to avoid a session timeout by extending the time limit via a simple user action.
Confirm that users are given at least 30 seconds to take action in order to avoid a session time out by extending the time limit of a session.

items: Pass: Users are given at least 30 seconds to extend the session.
Fail: Users are given less than 30 seconds to extend the session.
NA: No session timeout is present.

blocks.t: For iOS devices, all Xcode - Accessibility Inspector Audit tests pass during development
For Android devices, all Accessibility Scanner tests pass during development

items: Open your app in Xcode for iOS or Accessibility Scanner for Android.
Start the accessibility tool used on your platform.
Ensure that there are no automated errors present.
Pass: Zero issues are found OR issues found are determined to be false positives by Visa Accessibility.
Fail: One or more issues are found.
